solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Two allowed personal ornament

parts.note: a brace is a pair, as of game birds
to let is to allow or permit

explanation.surface: A pair of permitted pieces of jewellery, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrist band of gold or beads is a piece of jewellery worn on the person.

clue.text: Cricket stroke's finished with spin

parts.note: something off or over is finished, as in 'the match is off'
a spin in a car is a drive

explanation.surface: A batsman's shot is complete, put away with plenty of rotation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spin' looks like the bowler's craft but means a ride in a car. The shot is hit along the ground to the off side, in front of the batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, a drive played to the off side of the field is a standard batting shot.

clue.text: Twisted Romeo being ditched developed gradually

indicators.note: something ditched is thrown away, so the named letter leaves the word

parts.note: to twist round is to revolve, past tense
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's lover is dumped and the plot slowly unfolds.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that evolved grew or changed slowly over time, as species do.

clue.text: Fruit's finished before halfway point of 500 years celebration

indicators.note: the word stops just short of its middle letter, so its second half is cut away

parts.note: a quincentenary marks five hundred years

explanation.surface: Someone's produce was used up before a big anniversary party was half over.
explanation.walkthrough: QUINCENTENARY has thirteen letters; its middle one is the seventh, N, so stopping before it leaves the first six letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A quince is a hard, pear-shaped yellow fruit used for jelly and jam.

clue.text: Fool can upset comedian

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the word upside down, reading it from bottom to top

parts.note: a tin is a can
a wit is a clever, funny person

explanation.surface: An idiot may knock over a comic performer.
explanation.definitionFit: A nitwit is a silly, stupid person, an idiot.

clue.text: Company's preferred number one choice?

parts.note: a firm is a business company; the 's is a link
a favourite is the preferred one

explanation.surface: The business picks out what it likes best.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm favourite is the clear front-runner, the top pick, as in betting.

clue.text: Palmist put large amount of money on counter

parts.note: a fortune is a great deal of money
a teller counts things, such as votes or cash in a bank

explanation.surface: Someone betting a fortune on a gaming counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'counter' looks like a shop surface but is one who counts; 'put on' just places one piece above the other in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A palmist reads hands to predict the future, which is one way of telling fortunes.

clue.text: Aswan Dam? One very much older!

definitions.meaning: dam means mother, and Aswan is in Egypt, so an Egyptian mother
a preserved body from ancient Egypt is thousands of years old

explanation.walkthrough: The Aswan Dam is a famous dam on the Nile; here 'dam' is read as a mother, as with animals.
explanation.definitionFit: An embalmed ancient body from the Nile valley; dam and mum both mean mother.

clue.text: Estimated the value of grain and paid out

indicators.note: the abbreviation for paid is spread out around the grain, enclosing it

parts.note: PD is the usual abbreviation for paid
rice is a cereal grain

explanation.surface: A trader valued a cereal crop and then paid the farmer.
explanation.definitionFit: To price something is to set or estimate what it is worth.

clue.text: Yearn to go by roads in the lengthiest direction

parts.note: to long for something is to yearn for it
ways are roads, as in highways

explanation.surface: Wanting to travel along the longest routes.
explanation.definitionFit: Longways means lengthwise, along the longest dimension of something.

clue.text: Prevented clergyman making an appearance

indicators.note: the short word shows itself inside the longer one, appearing within it

explanation.surface: A vicar was stopped from turning up.
explanation.definitionFit: Rev, short for reverend, is an informal title or name for a priest or minister.

clue.text: Cores — get uncle to remove one

indicators.note: to re-move the letters is to move them again into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A request to have a relative take away a single item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remove' is read as re-move, shifting UNCLE's letters to NUCLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuclei is the plural of nucleus, the central core of an atom or cell.

clue.text: Sloths, armadillos, etc saying goodbye to paradise?

indicators.note: to here means attached to, so one piece comes straight after the other

parts.note: the Garden of Eden is paradise
ta-ta is a casual British goodbye

explanation.surface: Bidding farewell to heaven on earth.
explanation.definitionFit: Edentata is the old zoological order of toothless mammals including sloths, armadillos and anteaters.

clue.text: Diminutive part that's edible

indicators.note: part means only a portion of the word's letters is used

explanation.surface: A tiny piece that can be eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: A nut is a kernel that can be eaten, one kind of edible.

clue.text: Worry about the thing found in an old mattress

definitions.text: thing found in an old mattress

indicators.note: about means around, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: fear is worry or dread

explanation.surface: Fretting over what is stuffed into an antique bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Old mattresses and beds were stuffed with plumage from birds such as geese.

clue.text: Old woman insultingly labelled a bad speller!

definitions.meaning: a rude name for an ugly old woman
a witch, someone who casts evil spells

explanation.walkthrough: 'speller' is not about spelling words but one who casts spells.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an insult for an old crone and an old name for a witch.

clue.text: Escape through broken gateway

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Fleeing through a smashed gate.
explanation.definitionFit: A getaway is a flight or escape, especially after a crime.

clue.text: Mad exploit overshadowing learner's study of voting trends

indicators.note: in a down clue, standing over means placed above the next piece
mad means crazy or wild, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: L is for learner, as on British L-plates

explanation.surface: A crazy stunt that eclipses a student's research into elections.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overshadowing' works because this is a down entry: the scrambled piece sits above the learner's letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An exit poll asks voters leaving polling stations how they voted, to forecast the result.

clue.text: Beast devastating tent area

indicators.note: devastating means wrecking, so the letters are torn up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: An animal tramples a camping area.
explanation.definitionFit: An anteater is a toothless mammal that eats ants, so it is an animal.

clue.text: Picture made by university amateur going in for initial energy

indicators.note: going in for means taking the place of, so one letter replaces another

parts.note: a college is a university or part of one
E is the symbol for energy; initial picks the first of the two

explanation.surface: Artwork made at a university by a non-professional replacing early enthusiasm.
explanation.definitionFit: A collage is a picture made by gluing scraps of paper and fabric onto a backing.

clue.text: Sent off, goalie's run to enter women's area!

indicators.note: the letter goes inside the other word
something sent off is scattered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: goalie's gives its letters with the s
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A goalkeeper is sent off and runs into the women's quarters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sent off' looks like a football red card but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A seraglio was the harem, the women's quarters in an Ottoman palace.

clue.text: Take retribution for engineer briefly blocking street

indicators.note: a thing blocking a street sits inside it

parts.note: AVE is short for avenue, a street
ENG is a short form of engineer

explanation.surface: An engineer blocks the road to get even.
explanation.definitionFit: To avenge a wrong is to punish whoever did it, taking revenge on them.

clue.text: Hear someone conducting German songs

indicators.note: hear means the word is listened to, not read

parts.note: a leader is one who conducts or directs

explanation.surface: Listen to a conductor perform German art songs.
explanation.definitionFit: Lieder are German art songs, such as those by Schubert set for voice and piano.

clue.text: Later but not too late

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both eventually and soon enough to avoid being late.

clue.text: After Penny leaves, it's still a patch of ground

definitions.text: After Penny leaves, it's still a patch of ground

indicators.note: leaves means goes away, so the letter for penny is removed

parts.words: it's still a patch of ground
parts.note: a plot is a patch of ground
P stands for penny in British money

explanation.surface: Even when the penny is spent, the field is still there.
explanation.definitionFit: A lot is a plot or parcel of land, especially in American use.

clue.text: Sad beautiful girl on the phone one's seen in the woods

parts.note: to feel blue is to feel sad

indicators.note: a phone carries a voice, so the word is heard, not read

parts.note: a belle is a beautiful girl

explanation.surface: A gloomy pretty girl rings someone out in the forest.
explanation.walkthrough: BELLE sounds like BELL; bluebells carpet English woods in spring.
explanation.definitionFit: Bluebells are wild flowers that grow in woodland, a familiar spring sight.

clue.text: Fluid a palm's spilling

indicators.note: spilling means scattering, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: palm's gives its letters with the s

explanation.surface: Liquid spills from a cupped hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Plasma is the clear fluid part of blood.

clue.text: Regularly goes round disreputable group

indicators.note: round means turned about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gang that often does the rounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' looks like an every-other-letter signal but is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A rogues' gallery is a collection of criminals or rascals, originally police mugshots.
